findings.name: detectability
findings.message: All error mechanisms that flip observables also trigger detectors.

findings.name: sensitivity
findings.message: All detectors are triggered by at least one error mechanism.

findings.name: observable_coverage
findings.message: All declared observables are flipped by at least one error mechanism.

findings.name: probability_bounds
findings.message: All error mechanism probabilities are finite and strictly positive.

findings.name: duplicates
findings.message: Found 7 duplicate mechanism signature(s) across 7 distinct location(s). Distinct fault paths can legitimately share a (detector, observable) signature on multi-round circuit-level DEMs (signature collision); if this DEM was assembled by concatenating sub-circuit DEMs, the same fault path may instead be double-counted. The decoder-facing probability for a shared signature is the XOR-folded value p_eff = p1*(1-p2) + p2*(1-p1) (iterated for 3+), shown per group in the counter-example. 6 of 7 group(s) are mixed (mechanisms with different decomposition structures share only the merged signature — distinct fault paths, not true duplicates).

findings.name: correctability
findings.message: Every syndrome maps to at most one distinct set of logical observables.

findings.name: null_mechanism
findings.message: No mechanism has empty detector and observable support.

findings.name: high_probability_mechanisms
findings.message: Found 1 mechanism instance(s) across 1 distinct location(s) with probability > 0.3. On a low-noise device this is unexpected and may indicate that probabilities were summed (p1 + p2) instead of correctly combined (p1 + p2 - 2*p1*p2) when merging sub-circuit DEMs. Consider reviewing DEM generation code or passing a higher threshold to check_high_probability_mechanisms if high noise is intentional.

findings.name: boundary_symmetry
findings.message: Skipped: fewer than 2 logical observables (boundary symmetry requires ≥ 2).
